Research & capstone
Opila Research Group · Aug 2024 – Present
Advanced High Temperature Materials for Hypersonic Flight
Investigating oxidation behavior of refractory materials under extreme hypersonic reentry conditions. Operating at temperatures up to 2400°C using a microplasma resistive heating system to replicate leading-edge environments.
  • Analyzed oxidation behavior of over 75 pure tungsten samples in molecular and partially dissociated oxygen environments
  • Operated microplasma resistive heating system up to 2400°C, replicating hypersonic vehicle leading edge conditions
  • Tested and analyzed 30+ Kapton samples to quantify oxygen dissociation levels
  • Used SolidWorks and Converge CFD to model fluid-sample interaction inside the microplasma system

Capstone Project · Aug 2025 – May 2026
Rotating Detonation Rocket Engine Initiator
Led a three-person Thermochemical Simulations sub-team on design, build, and test of a scaled-down RDRE initiator. Engineered stability and reliability improvements through analysis of detonation wave behavior and geometric influence on wave propagation.
  • Designed, built, and tested a scaled-down RDRE initiator examining detonation wave behavior
  • Led thermochemical simulations sub-team — managing communication across sub-teams and advisor
  • Leveraged NASA CEA and Cantera to model chemical equilibrium and gas dynamics, optimizing experimental parameters and establishing robust, repeatable test procedures
  • Identified testing hazards, implemented mitigation strategies, and established comprehensive procedures for safe operation of a high-pressure detonation facility

Amateur rocketry · Summer 2025
Independent Project

Custom Thrust Stand &
Amateur Solid Rocket Motor

Designed and built a complete thrust measurement system from scratch — including a custom wooden test stand, 3D-printed motor mount hardware, an Arduino-based data acquisition system with HX711 load cell amplifier, hand-wound electric match igniters, and a homemade solid propellant motor. Conducted three live static fire tests with real-time force logging, achieving a peak recorded thrust of 25.75 N.

3D-printed components — SolidWorks 2023
All 10 components below were modeled in SolidWorks and FDM-printed for the project. They span four subsystems: propellant manufacturing tooling, motor hardware, load cell instrumentation, and stand structure. The load cell attachment went through two design iterations after v1 testing revealed off-axis loading artifacts in the thrust data.
Cylinder Cement Mold
Casting mold
Propellant Manufacturing
Printed shell used to cast quick-setting cement into a cylindrical form. The cured cement becomes the core mold for shaping the propellant grain's inner bore geometry.
📄 cylinder_cement_mold.SLDPRT
Propellant Mold
Grain casting
Propellant Manufacturing
Outer mold for casting and curing the solid propellant grain inside the PVC motor casing. Defines the outer diameter and ensures concentricity during cure.
📄 Propellant_mold.SLDPRT
Tamp
Packing tool
Propellant Manufacturing
Tamping rod used to compress propellant increments into the motor casing during casting, ensuring uniform density and eliminating voids in the grain.
📄 Tamp.SLDPRT
Propellant Funnel
Pour guide
Propellant Manufacturing
Custom funnel sized to the motor casing inner diameter. Channels propellant mix cleanly into the tube without spillage during the casting process.
📄 funnel.SLDPRT
1/4" Nozzle Cap
End closure
Motor Hardware
End cap for sealing the motor casing nozzle end during propellant casting and cure. Threaded 1/4" interface ensures a secure, leak-free press fit.
📄 one_fourth__cap.SLDPRT
Four-Inch Retention Bolt
Motor retention
Motor Hardware
Custom-length fastener for securing the motor casing to the stand fixture. Printed to exact length to allow alignment adjustability within the clamp assembly.

Load Cell Attachment v1
Force transfer
DAQ / Instrumentation
First iteration adapter coupling the S-type load cell to the motor casing base. Transfers axial thrust force cleanly into the load cell sensing axis.

Force transfer (revised)

Motor Stabilizer
Lateral constraint
Stand Hardware
Cross-arm clamp that laterally constrains the motor casing on the stand top plate. Adjustable via threaded bolts to accommodate different casing diameters.

Ground Stabilizer
Base anchor
Stand Hardware
Footer block printed to anchor the stand base to the ground surface during static fire, preventing recoil displacement and maintaining load cell alignment under thrust.
📄 ground_stabilizer.SLDPRT
Build process
01 — Hardware components: Arduino Uno, HX711 amplifier & S-type load cell
02 — Soldering the HX711 amplifier leads to the load cell wiring harness
03 — HX711 PCB: GND/DT/SCK/VCC digital side, E+/E−/A+/A− load cell bridge
04 — Hand-wound twisted-pair electric match igniters (nichrome bridge wire)
05 — Completed thrust stand: pine frame, 3D-printed clamps, load cell inline
06 — Motor casing seated in 3D-printed cross-clamp fixture, igniter wired in
07 — Side profile: load cell transfers motor thrust directly into frame base
08 — Homemade solid propellant grain cast and cured in PVC motor casing

About

I'm Spence Coleman Hartman, a B.S. Aerospace Engineering graduate from the University of Virginia School of Engineering and Applied Science (May 2026, GPA 3.796, High Distinction). I'm now matriculating into the Georgia Institute of Technology M.S. Aerospace Engineering program in August 2026.

As an A. James Clark Scholar — one of 21 in my class — I've been trained at the intersection of engineering, leadership, global experience, and business acumen. That's shaped how I approach technical work: with communication, context, and cross-functional awareness.

My research spans two active projects: investigating hypersonic reentry materials at the Opila Lab and leading thermochemical simulations for a Rotating Detonation Rocket Engine initiator team. Both demand rigor, precision, and the ability to operate equipment at extreme conditions.

Outside the lab I've served as a volunteer firefighter with the Seminole Trail VFD — 500+ hours responding to fire, medical, and MVA calls across Albemarle County.
